stories.headline: [Euronews.com] Europeans leave G7 feeling relieved, balancing self-interest and flattery to keep Trump in check Macron hailed the G7 as an "objectively successful" summit after leaders agreed on key issues from Ukraine and Iran to critical minerals.
stories.summary: The G7 summit concluded with European leaders feeling relieved after agreeing on key issues. French President Emmanuel Macron hailed the summit as "objectively successful" after three days of high-stakes diplomacy. Leaders reached agreements on issues including Ukraine, Iran, and critical minerals. The summit's success was attributed to the Europeans' ability to balance self-interest and flattery to keep former US President Trump's influence in check, although it is noted that Trump did exit. Despite challenges, the G7 nations were able to find common ground and reach consensus on several important topics, leading to a positive outcome for the summit. Macron's assessment of the summit as "objectively successful" suggests that the leaders were able to put aside their differences and work towards common goals. The agreements reached at the summit are expected to have significant implications for global affairs.

stories.headline: [The Catholic Times] Pope says Church ‘must move forward’ if SSPX proceeds with illicit ordinations Pope Leo also expressed his optimism about the recent deal to end the war in Iran that is expected to be signed June 19 in Switzerland.
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has expressed concern over the Society of St. Pius X (SSPX) proceeding with illicit ordinations, stating the Church "must move forward" in such an event. The Vatican had refused to give SSPX permission to consecrate its own bishops. Meanwhile, the Pope has also commented on the recent US-Iran agreement, expressing optimism that it will bring an end to the war. He hopes the memorandum, expected to be signed on June 19 in Switzerland, will be "truly a solution to the war" and allow for progress "for the good of all." The Pope's comments come after months of escalating violence in the Middle East, which he had previously addressed with "deep concern" following US and Israeli airstrikes. The Vatican's stance on SSPX and the US-Iran agreement reflects the Pope's efforts to navigate complex global issues.

stories.headline: [Al Jazeera] Tehran says considering plan for Iran, US presidents to sign deal Trump says he expects the agreement with Iran to be signed ‘shortly’ without specifying the exact date.
stories.summary: Iran is considering a plan for its president and the US president to sign a Middle East peace deal. US President Donald Trump expects the accord to be signed shortly, without specifying a date. The deal's details include the removal of the nuclear threat from Iran, with Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu stating that any final agreement must include the removal of enriched nuclear material from Iran. Trump has confirmed that the US-Iran peace deal is complete, and Iran's president has issued a statement in support of signing the memorandum of understanding. The deal reportedly includes the release of billions of dollars in Iran's frozen assets in the West. A $300 billion Iran reconstruction fund is also being planned by the US and its allies. The signing of the deal is expected to have significant implications for the region.

stories.headline: [Euronews.com] was selected for its G7 news, but a second selection is the news from [The Telegraph] is not as important as the news from [Al Jazeera] and [The Catholic Times], so the 4th selected news is [the-star.co.ke] 'No in-flight entertainment' as Red Arrows set off for US
stories.summary: The British Ministry of Defence is investigating reports that a Russian warship fired warning shots near a yacht in the English Channel. This development comes amidst the G7 summit, which concluded on June 17 in Italy's Puglia region. The summit was held from June 15 to 17, with a controlled access zone in effect from June 10 to 18. Meanwhile, the Red Arrows, a British aerobatic team, have set off for the US with no in-flight entertainment. The G7 leaders' summit was also scheduled to take place in Canada's Kananaskis Village from June 15 to 17, with a no-fly zone in effect. These events are unfolding simultaneously, with the Russian warship incident being the latest breaking news. The situation is being closely monitored and developed by newsrooms.

stories.headline: Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 Ports Are Coming to PlayStation in July
stories.summary: Call of Duty: Black Ops and Black Ops 2 ports are coming to PlayStation in July. Treyarch has officially confirmed the ports, which will include Campaign and Multiplayer modes. The release is expected mid-July, with some updates scheduled for July 2. Developer Iron Galaxy is handling the ports. This confirmation follows previous rumors and speculation about the classic games being re-released on the PlayStation platform. The ports will be available for PlayStation, likely including the PS5. The exact release date has not been announced, but it is expected to coincide with other Call of Duty updates, including Season 4 Reloaded on July 2 and Season 5 at the end of July.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches scheduled tasks in ChatGPT, details here
stories.summary: OpenAI has launched a new feature in ChatGPT called Scheduled Tasks, allowing users to set one-time or recurring tasks to be executed at specific times, even when offline. The feature is accessible through a new Scheduled page in the sidebar, where users can view, pause, resume, edit, or delete active tasks. Tasks can be created via the ChatGPT interface or through direct conversation prompts. This update enables ChatGPT to run prompts at preset times, automating reminders and tasks. The Scheduled Tasks feature is currently in beta and is rolling out starting today, marking a shift toward more proactive AI functionality in ChatGPT. Users can discover and manage their scheduled tasks in one place, making it easier to automate and stay organized with the help of ChatGPT. The feature is expected to enhance user experience and productivity.

stories.headline: Epic wants to let you bring your Fortnite skins to other games
stories.summary: Epic Games has announced plans to allow players to use their Fortnite skins in other games built with Unreal Engine 6. This move aims to break down barriers between different games, enabling players to use skins and cosmetics purchased in one game in other compatible titles. The feature will be made possible through Epic's Unreal Engine 6, a game development platform. Epic has already teased several crossover skins for Fortnite, and this new development could lead to further collaborations. Players will be able to use their Epic Games Account to access their skins across different games, but accounts cannot be sold, traded, or shared with others. The announcement suggests a shift towards a more interconnected gaming ecosystem, with Epic Games at the forefront of this change.

stories.headline: Electric Nose Detects Spoiled Food
stories.summary: UC Berkeley researchers have created an "electronic nose" that can detect gases produced by spoiled food and food allergens more accurately than human noses. The device uses carbon nanotube sensors and AI to identify spoilage and allergens. Its sensitivity is notable, able to detect as little as 0.05 grams of walnut, equivalent to one hundredth of a shelled nut. This technology has potential applications in quality control, food packaging, and field detection of contamination. Additionally, similar devices could be used to warn of natural gas presence or detect brain cancer cells. A related wireless tagging device can send signals to smartphones when meat and other perishables have spoiled, enhancing consumer and distributor safety. The electronic nose's development may help mitigate food safety hazards and improve detection of contaminants.

stories.headline: South Africa star to miss rest of World Cup group stage with three-game ban following red card against Mexico
stories.summary: South Africa attacking midfielder Themba Zwane has been suspended for three matches by FIFA following his red card against Mexico. The 36-year-old received a straight red card in South Africa's 2-0 opening match defeat. The suspension, subject to appeal, rules Zwane out for the remainder of the World Cup group stage. FIFA's disciplinary committee handed down the decision, which will keep Zwane sidelined for three matches. The suspension is a significant blow to South Africa's chances in the tournament. Zwane's absence will be felt as the team looks to recover from their opening loss and navigate the remaining group stage matches without one of their key players. The suspension is currently in effect, pending any potential appeal from South Africa or Zwane.

stories.headline: FIFA wanted Avalanche's blockchain to help curb World Cup ticket scalping
stories.summary: FIFA is utilizing the Avalanche blockchain to combat World Cup ticket scalping. The federation's digital collectibles and fan platform, FIFA Collect, is powered by the Avalanche network and Modex. A custom Avalanche blockchain is being used for ticketing, loyalty, and digital collectibles for the 2026 World Cup. This setup includes a dedicated Avalanche Layer 1, announced in May 2025. The move aims to curb ticket scalping, which has seen prices for the World Cup final spike to $11,000 per seat, prompting investigations by state attorneys general. The use of Avalanche's blockchain technology is a significant real-world test for the platform, and its adoption has contributed to an 8% increase in the AVAX price over 24 hours. The partnership also involves Kraken, further expanding the blockchain's reach.

stories.headline: Mother of Cape Verde star Vozinha will secure visa to attend World Cup in US
stories.summary: The mother of Cape Verde's star goalkeeper Vozinha, Ana Candida Evora, has been granted a visa to enter the United States. She will now be able to attend her son's next World Cup match, scheduled for Sunday against Uruguay. Initially, visa issues had prevented her from witnessing Vozinha's World Cup performance, including his team's draw against Spain. All necessary fees have been taken care of, ensuring Evora can secure her visa in time for the upcoming match. The 40-year-old Vozinha will have his mother in attendance for the game, following the resolution of the visa issues that had previously barred her from traveling to the US.

stories.headline: Liverpool urged to make a move for Marcus Rashford
stories.summary: Liverpool have been urged to make a move for Manchester United's Marcus Rashford, with former goalkeeper David James suggesting an audacious transfer bid. Rashford is currently on loan at Barcelona and has been linked with several clubs, including AC Milan. However, the player's preference is to move to a Spanish club. Manchester United have set a £40million asking price for Rashford, who has ruled out moves to Turkey or Saudi Arabia. Despite the interest, a deal for Liverpool to sign Rashford is considered practically impossible. Liverpool are in the market for a winger this summer, but Rashford's transfer preferences and Manchester United's asking price may prove to be significant obstacles in any potential move. Rashford's future remains uncertain, with several clubs monitoring his situation.

stories.headline: 'India always on the side of peace': PM Modi meets Zelensky in Evian during G7 Summit Taking to X, PM Modi said he reiterated that India will always be on the side of peace, "placing the values of humanity over everything else."
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Evian during the G7 Summit. Modi stated that India will always be on the side of peace, prioritizing humanity's values. The two leaders discussed restoring trade ties to pre-war levels. Modi emphasized India's commitment to peace, placing human values above all else. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 50th G7 Summit in Apulia, Italy, where Modi later traveled to Paris for further diplomatic engagements. The talks focused on reviewing bilateral relations and promoting peace, with both leaders agreeing on the need to revive trade ties. Modi's statement reiterated India's stance on prioritizing humanity and peace in its international relations. The meeting marked a significant diplomatic engagement between India and Ukraine, with Modi reaffirming India's commitment to peaceful resolutions.

stories.headline: Big trade wins for India as PM Modi attends G7 meet: UK deal date, EU FTA by year-end | Full list The timelines of two key trade deals for India were fixed, and US President Donald Trump also shared a big update on the ongoing trade negotiations with India.
stories.summary: India has secured significant trade wins as Prime Minister Narendra Modi attends the G7 meet. The India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement is set to be implemented from July 15, following a meeting between PM Modi and UK counterpart Keir Starmer. Additionally, the European Union has agreed to a free trade deal with India, aiming to create a free trade zone of two billion people by the end of the year. The US has also announced plans to slash reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods to 18%, with bilateral trade expected to reach $85 billion in 2024. These developments follow a series of trade agreements and negotiations, including a recent deal with Canada, strengthening India's energy security and expanding its trade relationships with key countries. PM Modi's meetings with world leaders, including US President Donald Trump, have yielded positive outcomes for India's trade landscape.

stories.headline: Seafarers issue of ‘utmost importance’: Modi to Trump Trump pledges U.S. support for India amid Modi's concerns over seafarer safety at G7 summit, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties.
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with US President Donald Trump at the G7 Summit in France, discussing key issues including trade, security, and regional stability. Modi emphasized the importance of ensuring the safety of Indian seafarers, who account for nearly 10% of the global maritime workforce. He urged Trump to prioritize their security, citing recent casualties. Trump pledged US support for India, stating that the US would be ready to assist in the event of any attack. The meeting aimed to strengthen bilateral ties, which have been strained by tariffs and recent incidents. Trump commended Modi's efforts to stabilize the region, and both leaders discussed ongoing negotiations and cooperation on issues like AI and maritime trade routes, including the Strait of Hormuz. The US president reiterated the great relationship between India and the US.

stories.headline: Bhagwat Says Maharana Pratap won Haldighati, questions historical narrative RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat says Maharana Pratap won the 1576 Battle of Haldighati, citing Mughal records and urging a rethink of historical narratives.
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat claims Maharana Pratap won the 1576 Battle of Haldighati, citing Mughal records. He urges a rethink of historical narratives, stating that false reports and tactics are being used to mislead. Bhagwat views the battle as a symbol of India's civilisational resistance, emphasizing its deeper significance in India's historical consciousness. He notes that while Raja Man Singh may have won tactically, Maharana Pratap's legacy lived on, and his kingdom and dynasty outlived the Mughals. Bhagwat considers the Mughal victory a "barren" one, as Maharana Pratap's name became synonymous with national resistance. He stresses that the battle represented the collective resistance of society, not just a military conflict. Bhagwat's comments aim to reframe the historical narrative surrounding the Battle of Haldighati and its significance in Indian history.

stories.headline: America's Loss to Iran Will Unravel Geopolitics Donald Trump is a man of his word: In March, the American president promised that “There will be no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER!... IRAN WILL
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a peace deal with Iran, claiming it will end Tehran's nuclear ambitions. The agreement comes after Trump previously stated that there would be no deal except for Iran's "unconditional surrender." The accord relies on commitments from Iran that have not yet been made, and it is uncertain whether they will be fulfilled. Despite this, the deal has been celebrated by the Trump administration and has boosted US financial markets. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian expressed willingness to end the war, but his role is subordinate to the country's hard-line clerics, who ultimately hold power. The US has not announced an immediate drawdown of forces near Iran, and the durability of the peace deal remains to be seen. The agreement's success depends on Iran's follow-through on its potential commitments.

stories.headline: Hot Mic Moments Catch Trump and Other G7 Leaders Mentioning Geopolitics and Greenland
stories.summary: At the G7 summit, a hot mic caught US President Trump mentioning "Greenland" in a conversation with European Council President António Costa. Trump said "You understand?" before pausing and adding "Greenland", although the start and end of the conversation were unclear. The comment drew attention due to Trump's long-standing interest in acquiring Greenland, a Danish autonomous territory, which has previously angered European leaders. Earlier, Trump was seen chatting with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, with whom he had appeared to have strained relations after the US-Israeli war in Iran. The leaders exchanged pleasantries, with Meloni insisting they had "always been friends". The hot mic moments provided a glimpse into the personal dynamics and discussions among world leaders at the summit, including geopolitics and trade. Trump's comment about Greenland sparked intrigue and speculation about his intentions.

stories.headline: Halki Returns to the Table: Erdogan, Bartholomew and the Geopolitics Behind the Seminary’s Reopening
stories.summary: Turkish President Erdogan has expressed willingness to reopen the Halki Seminary, a Greek Orthodox theological school closed by the Turkish government in 1971. Erdogan stated that Turkey is "ready to do whatever we can" after discussing the matter with Patriarch Bartholomew. The seminary's reopening has been a long-standing issue, with Bartholomew, Greece, the EU, and the US advocating for its restoration. The topic was recently raised during Erdogan's 2025 visit to the White House. Turkey has historically tied the seminary's reopening to the treatment of the Muslim Turkish minority in Greece's Western Thrace region. The US Congress passed resolutions supporting the seminary's reopening in 1998. The issue is seen as a strategic diplomatic matter, affecting Greek-Turkish relations and minority rights, with international attention and support for its reopening. Talks between Erdogan and Bartholomew were held in a "cordial atmosphere."

stories.headline: Geopolitics is complicating the green transition - and China’s moment
stories.summary: Governments seeking to transition to cleaner energy face a challenge in reducing their strategic reliance on China. The global energy system remains fragile, dependent on a few geopolitical chokepoints. China's dominance in the market is complicating the trade of global minerals and commodities. Indonesia, with the world's largest nickel reserves, relies on Chinese investment and technology to harvest and refine its stocks, crucial for battery manufacturing. The US is trying to counter China's technological ascendance, with bipartisan support in Washington. However, some in the Biden administration argue this stance is shortsighted. The conflict highlights the difficulty in balancing the goal of a green transition with the need to reduce dependence on China, making the path to cleaner energy more complex. Geopolitics is adding a layer of complexity to the already challenging task of transitioning to cleaner energy.

stories.headline: Shikha Mukerjee | Congress’ Fading Grandeur and Momentum of Inertia Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Congress, has been consistent in facing off against the BJP
stories.summary: The Congress party, as the main opposition in the Lok Sabha, has consistently faced off against the BJP. Upcoming Assembly elections in Maharashtra on November 20 will be a significant test for the Congress and the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance. The alliance includes the Congress and regional parties like the Samajwadi Party. It is expected that these parties will work together to avoid giving the BJP an advantage. The Congress and its allies are likely to cooperate, rather than work against each other, in order to maximize their chances of success. The Maharashtra elections will be a crucial indicator of the opposition's strength and ability to challenge the BJP. The outcome will have significant implications for Indian politics, particularly for the Congress party's fading grandeur and momentum.

stories.headline: Biden and Putin Engage in Heated Exchange Over Ukraine at G7 Summit
stories.summary: US President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin engaged in a heated exchange over Ukraine at the G7 Summit in France. The exchange occurred as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky pressed G7 leaders for more support in the country's fight against Russia. The summit did not bring a breakthrough on Ukraine, but it improved coordination between the US and Europe. Zelensky called out Putin as the obstacle to ending the war in Ukraine. Despite the lack of a breakthrough, Ukraine won key pledges of further support from world leaders attending the summit. The US-Iran deal and Russia's war on Ukraine were central topics at the summit, with leaders discussing ways to address the ongoing conflict. The exchange between Biden and Putin highlights the ongoing tensions between the two nations over Ukraine.

stories.headline: US Senate Passes Landmark Bipartisan Bill to Protect Same-Sex Marriage
stories.summary: The US Senate passed a landmark bipartisan bill to protect same-sex and interracial marriage, with a 61-36 vote. The Respect for Marriage Act would enshrine same-sex and interracial marriages in federal law, building on the 2015 Supreme Court decision in Obergefell v Hodges. Twelve Republicans supported the bill, which requires individual states to recognize another state's legal marriage, but does not set a national requirement for legalization. The bill follows months of bipartisan negotiations and is expected to be passed by the House before the end of the year, possibly as soon as next week. If enacted, the law would provide federal protections for same-sex marriage, ensuring that marriages performed in one state are recognized nationwide. The bill's passage marks a significant step towards cementing marriage equality in the US.

stories.headline: European Union Leaders Reach Deal on Landmark Climate Change Package
stories.summary: European Union leaders have reached a deal on a landmark climate change package, aiming to fight global warming. The agreement is part of the bloc's ambitious Green Deal, which outlines goals to reduce emissions and increase renewable energy use. Negotiators from the European Parliament and the European Council finalized the climate law, a key component of the package. However, the deal does not include mandatory renewable energy goals for individual member states, a decision that has been postponed. The agreement marks a significant step in the EU's efforts to lead the global fight against climate change, but critics argue it does not go far enough to address the issue. The deal is seen as a major achievement, but its implementation and impact will be closely watched in the coming years.

stories.headline: Stock Market Highlights June 17: Sensex gains 347 pts, Nifty closes at 24,085 on easing crude oil prices Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights - Find here all the highlights related to Sensex, Nifty, BSE, NSE, share prices and Indian stock markets for 17
stories.summary: Sensex gained 347.14 points to close at 77,155.62, a 0.45% increase, while Nifty rose 96.55 points to 24,085.70, a 0.40% gain. The increase was attributed to easing crude oil prices and improving market sentiment. The 30-share BSE Sensex opened with a 50-point gain, and the Nifty50 started 20 points higher. Throughout the day, the Sensex hit a high before closing 347 points up, and the Nifty50 ended 96 points higher. The gains reflect a positive response to the decline in crude oil prices, which has eased concerns about inflation and interest rates. The Indian stock markets, including the BSE and NSE, saw a notable uptick in trading activity, with key indices posting significant gains by the end of the trading session on June 17.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty extend gains as US-Iran peace deal cools crude oil prices Indian benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, extended their winning streak for a fourth consecutive session, driven by a significant drop in crude oil prices fol
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices, Sensex and Nifty, extended their gains for a fourth consecutive session. The surge was driven by a significant drop in crude oil prices following a potential US-Iran peace deal. The decline in oil prices eased concerns over inflation and boosted investor sentiment. As a result, the Sensex and Nifty indices continued their upward trend, with energy shares also rising. The drop in crude oil prices has a positive impact on the Indian economy, which is heavily reliant on oil imports. The peace deal between the US and Iran has led to a decrease in global oil prices, with US crude oil falling to $64.15 a barrel and Brent crude losing 96 cents. This development has contributed to the ongoing rally in the Indian stock market.

stories.headline: Stock market today: What are top gainers and losers in BSE Sensex and Nifty50 today? Check list India Business News: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty closed higher for a fourth consecutive session on Wednesday as softer crude oil prices following
stories.summary: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty closed higher for a fourth consecutive session on Wednesday. Softer crude oil prices, following the US-Iran situation, contributed to the positive trend. The BSE IT index rose 1.4%, with Subex, Magellanic, and ASM Technologies among the top gainers. The Nifty Oil & Gas index also saw top stock gainers during the intra-day session. The Sensex and Nifty50 closed in the positive territory, driven by investor focus on low global crude oil prices. This marks the fourth consecutive session of gains for the benchmark indices. Investors can track live stock market updates, share prices, and Sensex and Nifty live indices on various finance platforms, including Angel One, which provides real-time data and insights for informed investment decisions. The positive trend reflects the market's response to global economic developments and commodity price fluctuations.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Sensex Gains 347 Points, Nifty Closes Higher For Fourth Session Indian equity markets rise as Sensex and Nifty extend gains, broader midcap and smallcap indices outperform, defence and PSU bank stocks lead the rally
stories.summary: Indian equity markets rose for the fourth consecutive session, with the Sensex gaining 347 points to close at 77,155.00 points. The Nifty closed above 24,085, supported by gains in heavyweight stocks and a sharp rally in defence counters. Broader midcap and smallcap indices outperformed, with the Nifty Smallcap 100 rising 0.79% and the Nifty Midcap 100 gaining 0.52%. Defence and PSU bank stocks led the rally, while buying in Trent, BEL, and Infosys also supported the gains. Falling crude oil prices after the US-Iran peace deal improved investor sentiment, contributing to the market's upward trend. The positive global cues and easing crude oil prices further boosted the Indian equity benchmark indices, extending their winning streak to a fourth session.

stories.headline: CoinDesk: Here is how Coinbase plan to survive the crypto winter by ditching its reliance on trading fees Analysts say the exchange's push into derivatives, payments and infrastructure broadens its growth story beyond crypto trading.
stories.summary: Coinbase is shifting its focus to survive the crypto downturn by reducing its reliance on trading fees. The exchange is pushing into derivatives, payments, and infrastructure to broaden its growth story beyond crypto trading. Analysts view this move as a strategic expansion, allowing Coinbase to diversify its revenue streams. The company has launched new products to drive this growth, aiming to usher in the future of finance on its platform. This shift is also driven by the increasing investment in AI and related infrastructure, which is transforming the crypto landscape. By expanding into new areas, Coinbase is positioning itself for long-term growth and reducing its dependence on volatile trading fees. This strategy is seen as a key factor in the company's ability to survive and thrive in the current crypto winter.

stories.headline: Insurance Business: Construction faces compounding risks ahead of 2030, report warns Tight financing structures leave little room for project overruns
stories.summary: Construction projects face compounding risks ahead of 2030 due to tight financing structures, leaving little room for project overruns. A report warns that this could lead to increased costs and strain on the industry. The rising cost of insurance premiums is also deepening the housing crisis, affecting homeowners across the country. According to the Consumer Federation of America's Director of Housing, Sharon Cornelissen, the skyrocketing price of insurance premiums is exacerbating the issue. Poor project management execution can lead to increased costs, and the current financing structures may not be able to absorb these overruns. As a result, construction projects may be at risk of significant financial strain, highlighting the need for effective project management and risk assessment. The insurance industry is closely watching these developments.

stories.headline: TradingKey: Gold (XAUUSD) Is down 2.02% on Jun 17: What Changed in Supply and Demand? Gold prices dropped after the Fed signaled higher interest rates for the year.Reduced geopolitical tensions in the Middle East lowered demand for safe-haven gol
stories.summary: Gold prices dropped 2.02% on June 17 after the Federal Reserve signaled higher interest rates for the year. The decrease in gold prices was also attributed to reduced geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which lowered demand for safe-haven gold. Analysts remain bearish on gold, expecting prices to decline to $4,370.00-$3,816.01 by year-end due to ongoing geopolitical uncertainty and potential further interest rate hikes. Currently, gold prices stand at $4,324. The market had previously seen buyers on dips, but the Fed's signal has put pressure on gold quotes. Despite this, some signs of stabilization have emerged, with buyers defending key support zones. However, the outlook for gold remains uncertain, with investors closely watching the Fed's policy decisions. Gold had previously reached all-time highs in late 2025 due to weak Treasuries and fragile confidence.

stories.headline: Business Wire: AM Best Assigns Issue Credit Rating to Sammons Financial Group, Inc.’s New Senior Unsecured Notes AM Best has assigned a Long-Term Issue Credit Rating of “a-” (Excellent) to the $750 million 5.95% senior unsecured notes, due June 2036, issued by Sammons F...
stories.summary: AM Best has assigned a Long-Term Issue Credit Rating of "a-" (Excellent) to Sammons Financial Group, Inc.'s new $750 million 5.95% senior unsecured notes, due June 2036. The rating reflects the company's strong financial position and excellent creditworthiness. The notes are part of Sammons Financial Group's capital management strategy. AM Best has also affirmed the company's Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of "a-" (Excellent). The rating action is based on Sammons Financial Group's stable operating performance, solid capitalization, and experienced management team. The assigned rating indicates a low credit risk and a strong ability to meet financial obligations. The notes are scheduled to mature in June 2036, with a fixed interest rate of 5.95%.

stories.headline: OpenAI chief tells G7 to 'not cede responsibilities' to AI giants
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman attended the G7 summit, where he urged global leaders to take charge of artificial intelligence regulation. He emphasized that governments should not cede responsibilities to AI giants, instead championing the idea that they should oversee the development and implementation of AI. Altman's message was clear: world leaders should not surrender control over artificial intelligence to companies. The G7 summit, held in France, provided a platform for Altman to express his concerns and encourage governments to play a more active role in regulating AI. His remarks come as AI continues to advance and raise concerns about its impact on society, highlighting the need for effective governance and regulation. Altman's call to action aims to ensure that AI is developed and used responsibly, with governments taking a leading role.

stories.headline: AI executives gather at G7 as Europeans seek checks on U.S. dominance
stories.summary: Top artificial intelligence executives are gathering at the G7 meeting in France, where Europeans are seeking checks on American dominance in the AI sector. Executives from Google, Open AI, Anthropic, and Mistral AI are joining political leaders to discuss the issue. The meeting comes amid growing calls for tech sovereignty in Europe, with many expressing distrust of American companies' control over AI. The Anthropic episode has further fueled concerns, prompting Europeans to push for greater regulation and oversight of the AI industry. The G7 meeting aims to address these concerns and explore ways to promote a more balanced and equitable development of AI globally. European leaders are seeking to establish guidelines and standards for the development and use of AI, in an effort to reduce dependence on American tech giants.

stories.headline: Artificial intelligence takes center stage at the G7 meeting in France
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron urged wealthy democracies to collaborate on regulating advanced artificial intelligence systems at the G7 meeting in France. Top AI executives from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI joined leaders for a working lunch to discuss balancing AI adoption with risk limitation. The topic of AI was a major focus at the G7, with concerns over its potential impact on human dignity and society. Pope Francis also expressed concerns about AI's growing influence on humanity, citing threats to human dignity. The discussion on AI regulation and its implications is part of a broader agenda that includes investment deals, critical minerals, and immigration. The meeting aims to address the challenges and opportunities presented by AI and find ways to mitigate its risks while promoting its benefits.

stories.headline: Top AI leaders, including OpenAI's Sam Altman and Google DeepMind's Demis Hass
stories.summary: Top AI leaders, including OpenAI's Sam Altman and Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis, have been discussing the potential risks of artificial intelligence. Altman has warned of an existential danger, suggesting that AI could lead to a catastrophic scenario for humanity. Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, has also been involved in discussions about the future of AI. Recently, executives from leading AI companies, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, attended meetings to address concerns about the technology. Altman has acknowledged the advancements made by Google, and has cautioned colleagues about the potential dangers of AI. These discussions highlight the growing concern among AI leaders about the potential consequences of their creations, and the need for responsible development and regulation of the technology. The meetings and warnings from top AI executives underscore the importance of addressing the risks associated with AI.
